fire.note: The goods left in the square 'quickly vanished in the flames' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759); its wooden fence is taken to have burned with them.

value.note: WASHINGTON SQUARE, built by T-3689 for the 1871 scene: the open square on the North Side between Clark and Dearborn Streets, south of Mahlon D. Ogden's house. 'Washington Square had been filled with fugitives earlier in the night, but they had been compelled to flee, leaving their household goods scattered on the ground. These light goods quickly vanished in the flames'; 'the open square immediately south of it' is one reason Andreas gives that the Ogden house was ordinarily beyond danger (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759). The square is laid on today's Washington Square Park, between Clark, Dearborn and Walton Streets; its fence is reconstructed.

composition.note: Open ground inside a low wooden fence; the fence is reconstructed.

kind.note: An open square (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759): the walker reads it and lets the visitor walk in it; nothing in the mesh comes from it.

wall_material.value: A wooden fence round open ground

function.note: 'The open square immediately south of' the Ogden house (Andreas vol. 2, p. 759).

built.note: An open square before the fire (p. 759); when it was laid out is not researched here, and 1842 stands for it.
